title: Gen Z initiative holds nationwide demonstrations across Germany

tea.why: Young people are protesting against rising living costs, pressure on younger generations, and planned compulsory military service.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand better education, lower living costs, increased investment in education, and an end to compulsory military service.
tea.changed: Oct 31: Thousands joined nationwide demonstrations across 34 cities organized by the campaign group Gen Z regelt.

summary: Thousands of people across Germany joined nationwide demonstrations on Saturday as part of a youth-led movement organized by the campaign group "Gen Z regelt". The protests took place in over 30 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt, Munich, and Cologne. Demonstrators voiced opposition to compulsory military service, rising living costs, and demanded greater investment in education. Authorities reported that turnout was significantly lower than the 182,000 participants initially expected by organizers, with police and organizers offering differing attendance figures across various cities. While German authorities expected the demonstrations to remain largely peaceful, the federal interior ministry warned of potential attempts by extremist groups to exploit the movement, and some cities saw instances of pyrotechnics and localized disturbances.
response: German authorities stated they expected demonstrations to be largely peaceful but warned that extremist groups might try to exploit the movement.
